I think a lot of people misunderstand these masks. Take the N95. People think that means 95% of particulate matter is excluded from passing. No, it means that in the studies performed in the 90s by NIOSH, they decided that the certification criteria was a 95-percentile of 10% or less penetration.

In other words:

95% percent of the people wearing the masks at any given time can expect 10% or less particulate matter penetration

This is particularly important, given that SARS-CoV-2 has a particle size of roughly 70-90 nanometers.

One other interesting thing about that study was that it was performed in two separate trials. The N95 designation ONLY HOLDS for those who have a FIT TEST performed using specialized equipment.

Without fit-testing, average filtration for the group dropped to 77%.

There are a lot of clueless people speculating about the altimeter with todays date on it being some sort of sign of things to come.

Let me clue you all in - The date on the label is a due date for calibration, nothing more. They get calibrated every six months.

I am a parachute rigger and skydiver with over 20 years experience, and I train these very Marines on this very equipment you see in the video.

If you're wondering, the rig is called an MM, or MMPS, which stands for Multi Mission Parachute System, and its made by United Parachute Technologies, or UPT, also formerly known as Vector. The rigs can be configured to do 4 different type of jumps, HDPC (Hand Deploy Pilot Chute), SSD (Self Set Drogue), SLD (Static Line Drogue), and DBSL (Double Bag Static Line).

The altimeter is an Altimaster-2, and they've been around forever. They're used by both the military and sport parachutists for all types of jumps. They are considered old technology by todays standards as many of us now choose to use a digital or audible altimeter.

Not saying big things wont happen today, they might, time will tell, but the label on the altimeter is a calibration due date.
